claims.value: Straylight is an agent-first, user-owned portable context and durable-work layer. It preserves learned knowledge and live resumable state—including evidence, decisions, plans, artifacts, open questions, checkpoints, and next actions—so later agents can inspect provenance, revise work, and leave a better durable state; notes and retrieval are supporting mechanisms, not the product boundary.

Cumulative cached replay and uncached input are separate token measures; a cumulative replay total must not be interpreted as uncached per-case input. The evidenced one-shot BM25 regression baseline is 17/20 cases, 48/53 evidence items, and about 1,070 mean estimated tokens. The detailed cached-versus-uncached numeric artifact was unavailable in the scoped corpus, so no unsupported total was asserted.

The first persistent build slice is a typed, process-persistent workspace lifecycle: reopen a parent checkpoint pinned at revision N; refresh to N+1 and expose an explicit evidence/constraint diff; provide batched exact/lexical query and range-read operations with a pluggable semantic lane; then commit an immutable child checkpoint naming its parent and exact source references. The BM25 shell remains only a regression fixture.

The implementation transition passes only when a harness case creates a parent at N, introduces a known N+1 constraint, resumes without reconstructing the full corpus, exposes the delta, matches the direct-filesystem answer claims, and commits a source-linked immutable child—all in no more than four completed workspace calls. Metrics must separately report cumulative cached replay and uncached input, and exact/lexical retrieval must work while semantic retrieval remains pluggable.

Instrument cumulative cached replay and uncached input separately.
